view: This is a guide print, and the guide is two-sided. On FQ4 itself, Symbotic has landed at or above the top of its revenue range for four quarters (630 against 610-630, 676 against 650-670, 721 against 700-720). FQ4 revenue around $780-790M and positive FCF, as the late Q3 receipts arrive, are therefore likely, but a revenue beat has not lifted this stock in 3 of the last 4 prints, so it is mostly held. The part the price may not hold is the December-quarter guide. Consensus has FQ1'27 at $818-822M, +6% sequential. In each of the last three years the December quarter was the weakest sequential step: -8.2% (FY24 Q1 against FY23 Q4), -13.8% (FY25), +1.9% (FY26). The FY26 Q1 guide was set flat to Q4 ($610-630M against $618M) while every other quarter's guide midpoint stepped up 5-7%. Symbotic also guides below where it lands, and a guide midpoint below consensus has cost the stock before. That argues for a Q1 guide midpoint near $790-810M, under the Street. Three things weigh against it. Management said in August that FY27 sequential improvement is 'steady'. Walmart raised its own FY27 capex to about 4% of sales and signed the $6B extension, with $125M of funded development work that can show up as revenue early. And with 15-32% of float short, 10.8 days to cover and the stock still about 22% below its pre-August level, a clean guide plus a cash inflection could squeeze hard, as in November 2025 (+39%). The reaction history leans negative and the puts are bid, so the market already leans the way the seasonal argument points. Today's 16% beta rally also means the overnight move will carry index noise in a week when QQQ moved 5-7% a day. Net: a slight downside lean, well short of anything I would bet on.
unpriced: Possibly the December-quarter seasonality: a consensus of +6% sequential against three years of flat-to-down December quarters and a company that guides conservatively. But management's 'steady sequential improvement' language and the downside-paid skew mean I cannot show the price misses it, so I make no recommendation.

recommendation.reason: The one candidate mechanism is a December-quarter guide below the $818-822M consensus: three years of weak December quarters, a flat Q1 guide last year, and guide midpoints that sit under consensus. Against it are management's 'steady' sequential language, Walmart's raised capex and new $6B commitment, and a crowded short (about 10.8 days to cover) that can turn a modest guide into a squeeze. Options already pay for the downside, and market beta dominates the overnight window this week, so the edge is not large or clear enough to recommend.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A FQ1'27 revenue guide midpoint at or above about $820M with FQ4 FCF clearly positive (well above $100M) would make this an up print, probably a large one given the short interest. A midpoint near $790M or lower would confirm the downside lean.

self_critique: The seasonal argument may be stale. Walmart combined deployment phases in 2025 and now has a raised FY27 capex budget and a $6B extension, so the December-quarter dip may be gone (FY26 Q1 was already +2%). Sell-side analysts see the same seasonality and still model +6%, probably on management's guidance. The crowded short and the 33% drawdown since August mean even an in-line guide with strong FCF could gap the stock up 10-20%, as last November. Against that, the market already leans bearish (put skew, a history of negative reactions), so my lean adds little to what is priced.
